test-db.spec's MIGRATIONS_FOLDER === migrationsFolder() assertion depends on vitest running from the repo root; that is intended here but will break if the test cwd changes

watchlist.e2e 'opens without login' says it loads '/' 'not via beforeEach', but beforeEach has already opened '/'. The second page.goto still checks the server's status and that there was no redirect, so the test still works; only the comment is slightly off.

layout.e2e.ts, contrast.e2e.ts, header.e2e.ts and focus.e2e.ts still import signIn and SEEDED_MEMBER/SEEDED_DESIGN, which e2e/accounts.ts no longer exports. Those files are outside this task's list, so this is presumably another task's work, but the full e2e suite won't run cleanly until they are fixed.

alerts.e2e takes a snapshot of the notify_channel rows in beforeAll and puts them back after each test, so later spec files still see the seeded ntfy topic. This is only safe because playwright.config.ts uses workers: 1.

contrast.e2e keepingChannels deletes and re-inserts every notify_channel row; with foreign keys on, that cascade-deletes any price_drop_delivery rows, which are not restored. The e2e seed creates none today, so nothing breaks now.

header.e2e 'no auth chrome' matches 'Admin' and 'Account' without exact:true, so it rejects any link whose name contains those words (case-insensitive). That is stricter than the contract and fine with the current two-link nav.

declaredActions in src/routes/action-endpoints.spec.ts is a hand-rolled scanner that does not understand regex literals. A quote or brace inside a regex in an action body would throw it off. It fails loudly (an error or a list mismatch) rather than passing when it shouldn't, so it is safe as written but may need care when actions grow.

The CSRF block's follow-up check (the ntfy channel still shows 'Enabled') assumes no earlier e2e file has disabled or removed the seeded channel. Today that holds only because e2e/ files run before src/routes/** files with workers: 1. The snapshot comparison done inside the test (toStrictEqual(before)) is the check that does not depend on file order.
The control test with ORIGIN unset (a matching derived https://<Host> Origin is answered 400) correctly shows that only the Host guard can refuse the rebinding POST.

restart.e2e checks '£19.99' on /watches/<id>, but that is also the watch's own pricePence, so a lost second price_point would still pass. Only the £24.99 point proves price history survived the restart. Asserting the timeline row count, or giving the second point a price different from pricePence, would make the check real.

fresh-install.e2e uses spawnSync with a 30s timeout for the refuses-to-start cases, which blocks the Playwright worker's event loop while it waits. That is acceptable here because nothing else runs in that test.

restart.e2e passes PROTOCOL_HEADER=x-forwarded-proto alongside ORIGIN to get past the CSRF check, based on the claim that adapter-node ignores ORIGIN at runtime. That workaround is in the test only; the test_contract's ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:<port> is still set.
Ports with leading zeros (e.g. 'localhost:00080') are accepted as port 80; harmless for a loopback guard, but this case is untested
The reject table goes past the contract with 'localhost:0', 'localhost:65536' and leading/trailing-space rows, so the port-range check and anchoring are actually exercised

Removing alert.schema.ts and the per-user channel/watch signatures leaves e2e/seed.ts (inserts into alertChannel, watch rows with userId) and e2e/harness.e2e.ts (imports alertChannel, calls loadChannelConfig(db, key, design.id, 'ntfy')) broken; e2e is outside tsconfig so typecheck will not catch it, but `npm test` will fail until a sibling task rewrites them.

watches.ts insert switched from db.transaction to db.batch (to avoid SQLITE_BUSY on concurrent adds). The libsql batch is still atomic, and the id-collision test now proxies 'batch'. This is a behavioural change the task description does not mention.

0009/0010 only reject multi-user databases whose users collide on a channel kind or a product. A multi-user DB with disjoint kinds and products migrates silently and merges into one install. That matches data_scope ('unsupported') but is not a full refusal.

Channels sealed under the old per-user AAD survive 0009 but read as unreadable until saved again (documented in crypto.ts and tested in channels.spec 'legacy AAD or wrong key'). Upgraded installs will need their channel credentials re-entered.

0009's hand-added DELETE of config_enc IS NULL deliveries runs after the file's PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON. That is correct because the pragma is a no-op inside the migrator's transaction, and migrate.spec checks the result with pragma foreign_key_check.

The 'handle imports' assertion only collects specifiers from `from '...'` clauses. A bare side-effect import such as `import 'better-auth/svelte-kit'` would get past it, so the 'any subpath' contract line is enforced only for the named and type import forms.

The guard reads the Host header, not event.url, so it holds even when adapter-node builds the URL from ORIGIN. local-request.ts accepts exact loopback names only, with an optional port from 1 to 65535.
